asked_by: Madhav, 26 Oct 2026 (India chat): "we have to do research about this crossover ... where are the multiple points meeting and like what is a good buy call"
title: Moving-average and MACD crossovers, and averages converging: do they give a buy (or sell) call?
hypothesis: After a 50/200 golden cross, a 20/50 upward cross or a MACD(12,26,9) upward signal-line cross, forward returns beat ordinary days (and the opposite crosses are followed by weaker returns); the 50-over-200 state is a better time to hold the index; when the 20, 50 and 200-day averages converge, a bigger move (either way) follows.

data.index: silver/kite_index/day (NIFTY 50, NIFTY BANK) 2003-2023, via india.teachers_stock.index_panel (rows before 2024 only)
data.stocks: gold/teachers/stock_panel.parquet (adjusted daily bars of the liquid universe, to 2023-12-29); base = liquidity rank 1-250 that day
data.nothing_sealed: no 2024+ row and no sealed folder is read

definitions.sma: simple averages of the close (stocks: from the panel's dist_sma20/50/200, computed on each stock's full history)
definitions.gc / dc: 50-day average crosses above / below the 200-day average (today above, yesterday not; stocks: yesterday must be the stock's previous session); one event per index or stock per 20 sessions
definitions.x2050up / x2050dn: 20-day average crosses above / below the 50-day average; one per 10 sessions
definitions.macdup / macddn: MACD line (EMA12 - EMA26 of the close) crosses above / below its 9-day EMA signal line; stocks need 60 continuous sessions of warm-up; one per 10 sessions
definitions.state50gt200: index only: the 50-day average is above the 200-day (the golden-cross state), every session
definitions.converge: max(sma20, sma50, sma200) / min(...) - 1 under 2%: index = every session in that state; stocks = the first day entering it, one per 20 sessions
definitions.trend states (stock split): uptrend = Nifty above its 200-day; downtrend = Nifty below both its 50- and 200-day averages (india.teachers_stock.market_context)

outcomes.index: from the next session's close to the close h sessions later (an index cannot be bought at the close that made the signal): fwd20, fwd60; abs20 = |fwd20|
outcomes.stocks: buy at the next open, sell at the close h sessions later, net of the delivery round trip and the spread estimate (india/costs.py): net20, net60; abs20 = |gross fwd20|

statistics.index (market timing): india.teachers_stock.msplit: quarter-block means of 'on' sessions against quarter-block means of 'off' sessions, Welch t across blocks; dates = the smaller block count
statistics.stocks vs ordinary days (the random-entr: india.teachers_stock.level: event mean minus the mean of all base rows (every 5th session of every liquid-250 stock, plus the events) in the same quarter, t across quarters
statistics.stocks, the trade itself after costs: india.teachers_stock.absolute: the event's own mean net return, quarter means
statistics.verdict: india/registry.record standard rule; MIN_DATES 16 blocks per period (rare events such as index 50/200 crosses are expected to be INCONCLUSIVE and stay so)

bar.note: a new family 'technical'; k frozen at the 27 variants below
